summary: Streaming session stalls mid-generation when backend kernel swap coincides with HTTP/2 flow-control window pressure
description: Issue summary: Several customers (initially Finlyx Payments) reported SSE/WebSocket streaming sessions that stall mid-generation for long-form responses (~1k+ tokens). The stream remains open but no additional chunks are emitted for 10–90s before either resuming or the client timing out. Impact: Enterprise customer experienced degraded end-user experience during business hours, multiple sessions timed out and impacted SLAs. Environment: prod, eu-west; Hosted API behind our NLB + per-region nginx proxy layer; serving runtime on dedicated pools with mixed kernel versions. Observed: stalls correlate with spikes in kernel-swap events on serving-worker hosts and with sustained HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE backpressure on the edge proxy. Expected: continuous token stream with <200ms token inter-arrival for these responses.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer prompt that triggers long-form generation (approx 800-1200 tokens) against redwood/open-chat-medium-v1 in eu-west.
2) Send request via SSE endpoint from a client behind a corporate proxy (we used a controlled test proxy to simulate), with keepalive enabled and no reconnect logic.
3) Generate concurrent burst of 10 streams to exercise batching and kernel swaps.
4) Observe some streams stall mid-generation (no chunks for 10–90s) while the HTTP connection remains established.
5) Reproduce rate increases probability of stall when kernel swap/worker preemption occurs during in-flight batch processing.
logs: [2026-03-12T10:14:23Z] edge-proxy eu-west nginx: http2 stream 0x7fc4 window_exhausted, awaiting WINDOW_UPDATE
[2026-03-12T10:14:24Z] serving-worker-87 kernel: cgroup_v3: swap_preempt triggered for process 11842 (runner)
[2026-03-12T10:14:24Z] serving-runtime: worker 11842 evicting quantized-kv-cache for model redwood/open-chat-medium-v1 (active requests: 6)
[2026-03-12T10:14:24Z] serving-runtime: streaming: paused emission due to kernel-swap/evict; awaiting resume signal
[2026-03-12T10:15:09Z] client: SSE connection open, last chunk received at 10:14:24Z, no new chunk for 45s
[2026-03-12T10:15:10Z] edge-proxy nginx: retransmit window_update after 30s; flow-control burst suppressed by proxy keepalive coalescing
observed_behavior: Streams remain open but no tokens are emitted for extended periods. Some sessions resume after system recovers; others time out client-side. Stall probability increases under bursty concurrent streams and when serving-worker kernel preemption occurs.
expected_behavior: Streaming responses should continue to emit tokens without multi-second gaps; short internal backpressure should not cause 10s+ silent stalls.
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): Customer supplied client-side capture showing no FIN/RST — socket alive. Network traces show tiny TCP ACKs but no payload from server during stall window.

SRE/Edge (Noah): Identified repeated HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE depletion on the nginx layer around the same timestamps as client-observed stalls. Proxy had aggressive keepalive coalescing enabled which delayed WINDOW_UPDATE frames under certain patterns.

Runtime (Priya): Correlated serving-worker kernel swap logs with stall windows. When kernel scheduled long-running kernel-swap/evict operation, worker paused emission while it serialized KV-cache eviction and kernel state changes.

Hypothesis: Two independent backpressure mechanisms aligned — edge HTTP/2 flow-control prevented timely WINDOW_UPDATE (so server TCP send blocked), while serving-runtime paused emission during kernel-swap. Together they caused long silence even though connection stayed established.

Repro: We reproduced locally by forcing a kernel preemption on a worker and simultaneously setting nginx to coalesce WINDOW_UPDATE under test proxy mode; observed identical 20–60s stalls in 7/20 runs.
Related: This overlaps conceptually with SUP-171421 (http2-window-exhaustion) and SUP-257001 (inflight-latency-spike stalls) but is a distinct cross-layer alignment issue.
Slack thread: #support (thread: <https://slack.redwood/archives/C01234567/p167861>) contains traces and initial reports.
Github: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4567 contains a mitigation patch for emission preemption handling.
Confluence: Draft postmortem created for kernel-swap/flow-control interplay.

root_cause: Intermittent alignment of three factors: (1) serving-worker kernel-swap/quantized-KV eviction causing the runtime to pause emission for longer than intended, (2) edge nginx HTTP/2 flow-control window coalescing that delayed WINDOW_UPDATE frames and prevented TCP send progress, and (3) client environments (corporate proxies) that suppressed small window updates and avoided reconnect logic — combined to produce multi-second silent stalls.
resolution: Short-term mitigations applied (2026-03-13): reduced http2 WINDOW_UPDATE coalescing on eu-west nginx proxies; adjusted proxy keepalive settings to avoid delaying control frames; instructed SRE to increase http2 window metrics alerting.

Runtime fix (2026-03-13): backported PR #4567 to canary and prod which changes emission path to continue flushing partial chunks during KV eviction and avoids a single long pause; configuration toggles added to force best-effort token flushing during maintenance operations.
Customer guidance: Recommended client reconnection/heartbeat fallback and extended client-side streaming idle-tolerance for enterprise proxies while we roll out fixes.

Follow-ups created: INT-4012 to improve kernel-swap observability and limit long-running eviction on serving hosts; INT-4013 to add synthetic streaming tests that combine induced kernel pause + edge flow-control to detect regressions early.
Status: Fixes rolled out to eu-west and monitoring shows stall events reduced by ~92% in the 48h after changes. Customer confirmed improved UX and no further timeouts.
Postmortem: Scheduled for 2026-03-20 in Eng postmortem forum.
resolution_notes: Applied edge proxy config change and runtime emission fix; mitigation reduced incident recurrence by >90%. Customer notified and SLA remediation discussed (credit offered). Follow-up operational tasks assigned internally.
time_to_restore: ~27 hours from first report to initial mitigation (2026-03-12T10:14Z -> 2026-03-13T13:00Z)
